The rendering at rendering.c:15 is `(int32_t)*(uint32_t*)(stack_m40 + (uint64_t)stack_m16 + 1)`. Since 1e53fc79 the gate grades a timeout as `slow` instead of as an O0/O2 `ub` disagreement; it grades `slow` both inside the full run and alone (--jobs 1). The rendering is correct. It is slow at -O0 because the vectorised pmuludq loop is spelled as __uint128_t lane-merge chains, the known XMM lane noise (PE, and lane-induction recovery).

tests/gold/review.c::clang-O2::fill.cause: [P10 lowering] An unaligned movdqu store is spelled as a typed 16-byte dereference: `*(__uint128_t*)0x404054 = XMM1_2;` (rendering.c:26), and likewise at 0x404064 and 0x404074. __uint128_t requires 16-byte alignment and a __uint128_t effective type. The target is g_table+4 (int[16]), which is only 4-aligned, and movdqu has no alignment requirement. No effective-type or alignment proof is consulted (memory_renderer.rs:973-978). Unrelated known defects: the void function is rendered as uint32_t with a return value (critique:calls F8), plus XMM lane noise.
